No one wants to be told what to do by a stranger. It's not a very effective means of persuasion.

Imagine instead, if the commenter were to say something along the lines of "Hey OP, this website is morally corrupt for reasons X, Y, and Z. By directly linking to them you are implicitly supporting these activities by giving the site views and clicks. Many users here will likely downvote your post just because of the URL. Using an archive like this one would allow you to share the content without supporting the site."

That would be much more persuasive for several reasons. First, it gives the OP reasons for not supporting the site, rather than just asserting that they shouldn't. People like to know the reasons why before they do something. "That website is corrupt" isn't a complete reason without saying how they're corrupt. Moreover, it treats the OP as a friend who just needs some guidance, rather than as an enemy for daring to visit and share an unapproved website. Most people who post these links have no idea what they're supporting, and they're not doing it maliciously or intentionally. They'd probably agree about archiving it, if they only knew. There's no reason to treat them as an enemy combatant. And beyond all of that, it avoids the imperative mood entirely. People don't like being told what to do, especially by a stranger on the internet who gives them no concrete reason to do so. If however, you ask nicely, and tell them why you want it, you might be surprised by how much more likely people are to respond positively.

There are also good reasons not to want to use an archive. Many pages don't archive well. I can't tell you how many archive.is links I've clicked that had little more than the background of the website, and failed to capture the video that was the centerpiece of the page. Some websites' formatting causes text to be illegibly distorted or pushed behind images during the archiving process. Beyond the technical errors that can be introduced, some parts of the page that update regularly, such as comments sections or leaderboards, are not updated in the archive. News articles about ongoing events are frequently updated as new information becomes available. The archive of these pages does not get updated, and it can be a hassle to re-archive it every time the article is updated.

And for anyone who has read this far, and doesn't already know, archiving a site is stupid easy. It's as simple as copying the link, and pasting it in a box on the archive site. Anyone can do it.
